---
title: "SPEC-4.1.1-v001"
subtitle: "Stable row order when closing tabs"
---

## Problem

In detail view, closing a tab (especially the top one) sometimes reshuffled
the remaining rows. Cause: closing a tab makes Chrome activate a
neighboring tab, which updates that tab's `lastAccessed` timestamp; the
resulting refresh re-sorted the list (default sort is "Last Accessed,
newest first"), so the newly-activated tab jumped to the top — reordering
rows right under the user's cursor. The same reshuffle could happen from
any background tab activity while the list was open.

## Behavior change

The **visible row order is now frozen**. It re-sorts only when the user
takes an explicit action:

- changing the sort column or direction (including the AI-group "Sort All"
  menu — repeating the same field forces a fresh re-sort),
- changing the view, window filter, sidebar selection, or search
  query/scope,
- pressing the **Refresh** button (its tooltip is now
  "Refresh & re-sort tabs").

Between those actions:

- closing a tab simply removes its row — nothing else moves;
- newly opened tabs append at the bottom of the list;
- cell contents (title, "last accessed" label, favicon) still update live —
  only the *order* is pinned.

## Implementation

- `App.tsx`: `currentDisplayedTabs` keeps a ref of the last row order plus
  a context key (sort + filters + search + a `resortEpoch` bumped by the
  Refresh button). While the key is unchanged, fresh tab data is re-mapped
  onto the remembered order; when it changes, the list re-sorts and the
  order is re-snapshotted. This also stabilizes card view and keyboard
  navigation, which share this list.
- `TabListView.tsx`: in controlled mode the table now renders the parent's
  (already stabilized) order verbatim instead of re-sorting it — the
  previous internal re-sort would have overridden the freeze. Uncontrolled
  tables (AI-group view) apply the same freeze internally, keyed by their
  own sort state and the `forcedSort` timestamp.

## Version

`package.json` / `manifest.json` bumped **4.1.0 → 4.1.1**.
